## Why it matters internationally

LNE is France's national metrology institute. Its MATIS thermal-characterisation
platform offers SI-traceable measurements of directional spectral emissivity from
250 nm to 20 µm and calorimetric total hemispherical emissivity. LNE's
reflectometer-based emissivity work goes back to at least 2005, validated against
PTB and NIST references, and a directional spectral emissivity facility working up
to 1500 °C was reported in 2013. LNE coordinated the European metrology project
EMIRIM (16NRM06, 2017–2020) on emissivity of reflective insulation, and Hi-TRACE
(17IND11) on traceable high-temperature thermophysical properties.

## Scope of activity

- **Quantities:** directional spectral emissivity (from spectral directional hemispherical reflectance) · total hemispherical emissivity (calorimetric) · normal spectral emissivity at high temperature · solar absorption factor
- **Spectral range:** 250 nm to 20 µm (directional spectral emissivity, at 12°, 24°, 36°, 48° and 60°)
- **Temperature:** Total hemispherical emissivity −20 °C to 200 °C (calorimetric); directional spectral emissivity facility up to 1500 °C (Hay et al., 2013)
- **Methodology:** SI-traceable directional spectral emissivity of opaque solids derived from spectral directional hemispherical reflectance (expanded uncertainty 0.025–0.04); calorimetric total hemispherical emissivity in vacuum; a high-temperature directional spectral emissivity facility with lamp-image-furnace or inductive heating.
- **Named facilities:** Spectral directional hemispherical reflectance / directional spectral emissivity bench · Calorimetric total hemispherical emissivity bench

**Application domains:** aerospace, defence, nuclear and transport materials · reflective and low-emissivity thermal insulation for buildings · high-temperature materials for aeronautics and energy.
